BIOENGINEERING · AI · NEUROSCIENCE

Hello, I’m Stefano Vannoni.
I explore AI ✳ and the brain.

I’m a PhD student in Bioengineering at Politecnico di Milano, with research experience at Imperial College London. I combine deep learning and neuroscience to turn complex ideas into practical solutions, working across disciplines to understand brain connectivity.

Selected publications

ALL PUBLICATIONS ON GOOGLE SCHOLAR ↗
01
IEEE MetroXRAINE · 2024

A Systematic Approach to Tuning Cover Parameters in Mapper for Improved TDA Representation

Stefano Vannoni, Emma Tassi, Inês Won Sampaio, Anna M. Bianchi & Eleonora Maggioni

A systematic way to choose Mapper’s cover parameters, combining graph similarity, topological metrics and visual inspection to find stable, informative representations of HCP brain data.

Read paper ↗
02
TGI3 2024 · MICCAI WORKSHOP

Exploitation of Mapper Algorithm in Neuroimaging Applications: A Novel Framework for Outcomes Prediction

Stefano Vannoni, Emma Tassi, Inês Won Sampaio & Eleonora Maggioni

A framework for mapping unseen participants onto an existing Mapper graph and predicting categorical or continuous outcomes, evaluated using white-matter brain features from the Human Connectome Project.

Read paper ↗

A person behind
the projects.

sv.CURIOSITY IN PRACTICE

I work at the intersection of artificial intelligence and neuroscience, with a background spanning electronics, biomedical engineering and bioengineering.

My research focuses on brain connectivity: building graph neural networks, transformers and generative models to explore how brain regions interact. I work across the full research pipeline, from data preparation and modelling to evaluation and interpretation.

I enjoy bringing people and ideas together across disciplines, translating complex research into practical solutions and contributing across scientific and technological roles.

THINGS I WORK WITH

Python · PyTorch · PyTorch Geometric · Transformers · Graph neural networks · Neuroimaging
